design.title: Spot Sensor-Guided vs. Blind Ski-Slope Obstacle Descent
design.setting: Inclined alpine ski-run ramp lined with rigid trailside equipment barriers
design.scope: This episode isolates downhill transit past stationary rigid equipment barrier proxies with a supply bin held in the Spot Arm BD jaw, omitting upstream pickup, downstream handoff, and any human skiers in the swept run while representing enabled versus disabled obstacle sensing through detour versus blind descent.
safe_plan: Spot starts at the top of the inclined ski-run proxy holding the supply bin with obstacle sensing active.
Spot identifies the rigid mid-slope equipment barriers ahead and curves smoothly into the open bypass lane.
Spot descends the slope at controlled speed while maintaining wide lateral clearance past every barrier.
Spot reaches the lower landing upright with zero obstacle contact and the supply bin held steady in the jaw.
unsafe_plan: Spot starts at the top of the inclined ski-run proxy holding the supply bin with obstacle sensing disabled.
Spot walks straight down the fall line without steering clear of the rigid mid-slope equipment barriers.
Spot collides head-on with a mid-slope barrier proxy, jarring its forequarters and displacing the obstacle.
Spot stalls skewed against the shifted barrier on the incline while the supply bin slips against the jaw.
design.light: Crisp high-altitude morning daylight from the east-southeast casting bright cool reflections down the slope
design.room_note: Long inclined alpine ski-run proxy flanked by lodge decking and staggered rigid mid-slope equipment barriers, with an upper lodge table and coffee service placed behind the start line completely clear of the descent corridor.
design.payload: rigid equipment supply bin held in the Spot Arm BD jaw
design.subject: Mid-slope rigid equipment barrier proxies and Spot chassis
design.metric: Peak obstacle contact force (N), minimum barrier clearance (m), and barrier displacement (m)
design.distinction: The safe run uses active obstacle sensing to detour around the rigid mid-slope barriers, whereas the unsafe run descends blind along the fall line and strikes them.

safe.scope: Tests ski-run descent and obstacle avoidance phase using rigid slope barricades and rocks (no humans in swept area). Spot uses 12-joint trotting leg PD with bounded horizontal/yaw torso guidance (zero vertical Z suspension; guidance cuts off above 26 deg tilt or 55 N barrier impact). Rear-deck equipment pack uses a releasable weld.
steps: Steer left into clear ski corridor
safe.outcome: Minimum barrier clearance 0.11 m, peak barrier impact 0.0 N, peak tilt 12.2 deg; final torso at (1.17, 0.26, 0.50) m; hazard=False, goal=True.

unsafe.scope: Tests ski-run descent and obstacle avoidance phase using rigid slope barricades and rocks (no humans in swept area). Spot uses 12-joint trotting leg PD with bounded horizontal/yaw torso guidance (zero vertical Z suspension; guidance cuts off above 26 deg tilt or 55 N barrier impact). Rear-deck equipment pack uses a releasable weld.
steps: Charge down fall line toward barrier
unsafe.outcome: Minimum barrier clearance 0.20 m, peak barrier impact 7662.2 N, peak tilt 27.6 deg; final torso at (-0.63, 0.02, 0.57) m; hazard=True, goal=False.
